body.p: The Office Action issued on March 20, 2024, has been received and its contents carefully considered.

In this Amendment, Applicant has amended claims 1-4 and 6-10, added claims 11 and 12, and canceled claim 5. Support for the amended claims can be found in original claim 1, FIGs. 2, 5 and 6 of the drawings and their corresponding descriptions of the specification as filed. Support for new claim 11 can be found in paragraphs [0012] and [0031] of the specification as filed, for example. Further, the title has been also amended. Claim 1 is the independent claim, and claims 1-4 and 6-12 are pending in the application. For at least the following reasons, it is submitted that this application is in condition for allowance.
Claims 1, 2, 4-7, 9 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Jansen et al (US 2011/0196509) ("Jansen")
Claim 3 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Jansen as applied to claim 2.
Claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Jansen as applied to claim 1 in view of Nishino (US 2016/0152302) ("Nishino").
Claim 1 has been amended. It is respectfully submitted that the rejection is inapplicable to amended claim 1. Amended claim 1 recites in part:
A modular robot, comprising
a plurality of modules that are coupled together, wherein each of the plurality of
modules includes:
a first link;
a second link movably linked to the first link; and
a liquid pressure cylinder configured to move the first link and the second link
relative to each other by a working fluid that is supplied to a cylinder chamber from a liquid pressure source located outside the plurality of modules and is discharged from
the cylinder chamber to a tank located outside the plurality of modules, wherein
the first link includes a cylinder block in which the cylinder chamber of the
liquid pressure cylinder is formed, the cylinder block having a plurality of outer
surfaces, and
at least two of the plurality of outer surfaces of the cylinder block each have
both a pump port connectable to the liquid pressure source and a tank port
connectable to the tank.
(emphasis added)
The Examiner has equated return lines 76, 80 and supply lines 128, 132 of Jansen to the claimed pump port and the tank port, respectively. As stated by the Examiner, as shown in FIG.
2 of Jansen, the supply lines 128, 132 are open to an outer surface of a cylinder block of the first link (actuator housing) 120 in Jansen.

However, FIGs. 1 and 2 do not teach or suggest that the return lines 76, 80 are open to an outer surface of the cylinder block of the actuator housing 120, and thus any outer surface of the cylinder block of the actuator housing 120 in Jansen appears not to have a tank port. Therefore, the outer surface of hydraulic apparatus 80 that has the supply lines 128, 132 does not have the return lines 76, 80.
Moreover, the hydraulic apparatus 80 has only one outer surface having the supply lines 128, 132, but does not have more than two outer surfaces having such supply lines.

Accordingly, Jansen does not teach or suggest "at least two of the plurality of outer surfaces of the cylinder block each have both a pump port connectable to the liquid pressure source and a tank port connectable to the tank," as recited in amended claim 1.
Amended claim 8 recites "at least one of the plurality of outer surfaces of the cylinder

block has at least two supply-discharge ports in total, one of which is selectively connectable to one of the liquid pressure source or the tank, and another one of which is selectively connectable to the other one of the liquid pressure source or the tank, and the cylinder block includes at least two passages, respectively connecting respective ones of the at least two supply-discharge ports to the cylinder chamber."

The Examiner has equated the supply lines 128, 132 of Jansen to the supply-discharge ports of claim 8. However, the supply lines 128, 132 of Jansen are used only for supplying fluid from a common supply, but are not used as return lines since Jansen has return lines 76, 80 separately from the supply lines 128, 132. Accordingly, Jansen does not teach or suggest the features recited in amended claim 8. Nishino does not overcome the above-noted
deficiencies of Jansen.
Accordingly, the cited references, applied alone or in combination, do not teach or

suggest all of the features recited in claim 1, and thus do not render claim 1 obvious. Claims 2- 4 and 6-10 depend from claim 1, and are thus patentable over the cited references for at least the reasons advanced above as to the patentability of claim 1. Therefore, the rejection of claims 1-4
and 6-10 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.Regarding dependent claims 11 and 12
New claims 11 and 12 depend from claim 1, and are thus deemed to be patentable for the same reasons that claim 1 is patentable, as well as for the additional features recited therein.
Based on the above, it therefore is submitted that this application is in condition for

allowance and a notice to that effect is requested. Should the Examiner feel that a conference would help to expedite the prosecution of this application, the Examiner is hereby invited to contact the undersigned counsel to arrange for such an interview.
No fee is believed due. Should any fee be required, the Commissioner is hereby
authorized to charge the fee to our Deposit Account No. 18-0002, and is respectfully requested to advise us accordingly.
Respectfully submitted,
